instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Temperature-controlled logistics provider operating 50 refrigerated trucks and 8,000 m² of cold storage warehousing. Specialize in pharmaceutical and fresh food distribution across Iberia. Evaluating real-time temperature monitoring sensors and predictive cold-chain failure alerting. The organization has significant capital, talent depth, and existing technology infrastructure, but internal processes are designed for stability and risk management — not speed. Innovation initiatives must navigate procurement, legal, compliance, and IT security review before receiving green-light. The key challenge is not resource availability but organizational velocity.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: We operate in a consolidating market where competitors are merging to gain economies of scale. Our independent position is increasingly vulnerable. We need to proactively strengthen our competitive positioning — either by deepening our specialization in high-margin niches where scale matters less, or by building platform-like switching costs that make our offering stickier for existing customers.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization. A group innovation fund of €5M annually is allocated competitively — business units pitch for funding against clear innovation KPIs including revenue from new products and process efficiency gains.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.

input.changes_since_last: Post-merger integration underway. Team doubled to 7 members. Culture clash between legacy and new teams.

opportunities.title: Unified Operational Blueprinting and Process Redesign (Post-Merger)
opportunities.rationale: The merger presents a unique, time-sensitive opportunity to redesign core processes rather than patching duplicative legacy systems. Focus must be on creating a single 'golden process' for logistics execution, invoicing, and compliance across the combined entities.

first_actions: Establish a cross-functional Integration Process Task Force (IPTF) with executive sponsorship to mandate process standardization.
Conduct comprehensive Value Stream Mapping (VSM) on 2-3 critical end-to-end processes (e.g., Order-to-Cash) across both legacy systems, identifying key pain points and duplications.
Develop a phased governance structure that mandates legal/compliance review sign-off before any process change is adopted.
resources_needed: Dedicated SME time from both legacy teams
Executive mandate for temporary process 'freeze' on redundant steps
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in manual handoffs or data entry points by 25% within the target processes.
milestones: Pilot testing of the new process flow on a small, contained business unit.

opportunities.title: Deep Dive into Niche Service Lines (Pharmaceutical Cold Chain)
opportunities.rationale: To strengthen market defense without massive capital expenditure, Synapse should deepen specialization in the highest-margin niche (pharmaceuticals). This allows for building 'stickiness' by optimizing unique compliance processes that competitors cannot easily replicate.

first_actions: Conduct a profitability deep dive, segmenting revenue by specific pharmaceutical client type/drug category to pinpoint the most profitable niche.
Develop specialized service protocols (SOPs) centered around this top-tier niche that incorporate real-time monitoring data and predictive alerting.
Design limited pilot offerings for key clients in this niche, positioning them as a premium, highly compliant service.
execution_plan.success_metric: Identification and formal proposal of at least two new, high-margin service packages.
milestones: Signed Letter of Intent for pilot program with a target client.

next_steps.action: Formalize the Integration Process Task Force (IPTF) charter and secure executive buy-in/mandate, ensuring representation from all major business units.
Initiate the Value Stream Mapping (VSM) workshops for the Order-to-Cash process, focusing on identifying points of duplication between the legacy and merged CRMs.
Schedule deep-dive customer interviews focused exclusively on high-compliance, niche pharmaceutical needs to validate the strategic focus for opp_4.

key_weaknesses: Fragile Cultural Integration: The clash between legacy and new teams remains a significant barrier to process standardization and adoption.
Process Duplication & Technical Debt: Multiple overlapping systems (CRMs, HR) prevent standardized execution and slow organizational velocity.
Governance Bottleneck: Innovation still relies heavily on linear review processes (legal, compliance, IT security), slowing time-to-market.

improvements: Digital maturity increased from 2 to 3, indicating better foundational technology infrastructure and resource allocation.
The merger has provided the structural opportunity to redesign processes entirely, moving beyond simple remediation of old flaws.
persistent_gaps: Cultural buy-in for change remains weak; success depends on overcoming organizational inertia rather than just completing technical steps.
No centralized 'single source of truth' process yet exists across the combined entity.
achieved_milestones: Completion of initial systems and team integration efforts (Milestone: Merger completed 4 months ago).
Successful completion of defined process steps (step_2).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The organization has achieved a clear increase in digital maturity (2->3) and successfully navigated a major merger. The focus shifts from resource constraint to systemic process redesign and cultural alignment.
